heroHeadline: Russia-Aligned Kambolov Claims Tskhinvali 'Presidency' as Georgia, EU, UK Reject Vote; Tbilisi Protests Reach Day 660
heroSubtitle: Russian official Marat Kambolov won Russian-occupied Tskhinvali's Sept. 18 'presidential vote' with 84.95% under a treaty deepening Russia-South Ossetia integration, a result Georgia's Foreign Ministry, the EU and the UK all reject as void and a step toward de facto annexation. The same week, Tbilisi and Batumi protesters marked their 660th consecutive day of demonstrations and announced a Sept. 27 march to Heroes Square commemorating the fall of Sukhumi, while PM Irakli Kobakhidze said the State Grant Management Agency created amid the NGO funding crackdown will close by year-end, calling NGOs "an artificial phenomenon." Separately, the Court of Appeals approved plea deals freeing three more October 4, 2025 unrest defendants, including a 72-year-old doctor released straight from the courtroom.
